title: Axiom Audit: One Proved, Three Deep
content: The file's header docstring doubles as a proof audit. Of the four axioms in the parent Erdos1007Problem.lean, one (hasUnitEmbedding_exists) is proved here via an explicit construction. The other three encode theorems from the literature whose proofs require case analysis on graph structures and geometric rigidity arguments. A key finding: the original axiom was logically incorrect — it asserts every finite graph has a unit distance embedding, but fails for graphs with self-loops (where dist(v,v) = 0 ≠ 1). The corrected theorem adds an irreflexivity hypothesis, which holds for all graphs arising in the context of Erdős #1007.
mathContext: $\text{hasUnitEmbedding}(V, \text{adj}, n) \iff \exists f: V \to \mathbb{R}^n,\; \forall u, v,\; \text{adj}\, u\, v \Rightarrow \|f(u) - f(v)\| = 1$; bug: $\text{adj}\, v\, v \Rightarrow \|f(v)-f(v)\| = 0 \neq 1$

title: Key Calculation: Scaled Basis Vectors Have Unit Pairwise Distance
content: The private lemma scaled_basis_sq_dist is the heart of the construction. Given two distinct indices i ≠ j in Fin n, the sum Σ_k ((δ_{ik}/√2) − (δ_{jk}/√2))² = 1. The proof proceeds in three steps: (1) all terms except k=i and k=j are zero; (2) the terms at k=i and k=j each contribute (1/√2)² = 1/2; (3) the total is 1/2 + 1/2 = 1. The proof uses Finset.add_sum_erase to extract the two non-zero terms, then simplification with simp and linarith for the arithmetic. The positivity of √2 is established via Real.sqrt_pos_of_pos.

title: Main Theorem: Scaled Basis Construction Proves Unit Embedding Existence
content: hasUnitEmbedding_exists_irr constructs the unit distance embedding explicitly: given a finite graph with vertex type V and irreflexive adjacency, use the bijection φ : V ≃ Fin |V| (from Fintype.equivFin) to map each vertex v to a vector in ℝ^|V| with exactly one nonzero component: f(v)_k = 1/√2 if φ(v) = k, else 0. For an edge (u, v) with u ≠ v, the vertices are mapped to distinct standard basis positions (φ u ≠ φ v by injectivity), so scaled_basis_sq_dist applies to give ‖f(u) − f(v)‖ = 1. The irreflexivity hypothesis is used exactly once: to deduce u ≠ v from adj u v, then φ u ≠ φ v by injectivity of φ.

title: Corollary: Complete Bipartite Graphs Always Embed as Unit Distances
content: The complete bipartite graph K_{m,n} has vertex type Fin m ⊕ Fin n with completeBipartiteAdj connecting every left vertex to every right vertex (and vice versa). This adjacency is irreflexive: a Sum.inl vertex connects only to Sum.inr vertices, so adj v v is false for all v. completeBipartiteAdj_irrefl proves this by cases on v ∈ Fin m ⊕ Fin n using simp. The corollary completeBipartite_has_embedding then immediately follows from hasUnitEmbedding_exists_irr. In particular, K_{3,3} admits a unit distance embedding, which is necessary for it to be a graph of finite dimension.
mathContext: $K_{m,n} = (\text{Fin}\, m \oplus \text{Fin}\, n,\; \text{completeBipartiteAdj})$; $\neg\,\text{completeBipartiteAdj}\, v\, v$ for all $v$ $\Rightarrow$ $\exists d,\; \text{hasUnitEmbedding}(K_{m,n}, d)$

title: Deep Remaining Axioms: Literature Classification
content: The summary section classifies the three remaining deep axioms: min_edges_dimension_4 (House 2013: any graph with dimension exactly 4 has ≥9 edges), k33_unique_minimum (House 2013: K_{3,3} is the unique such graph up to isomorphism), and min_edges_dimension_5 (Chaffee-Noble 2016: dimension-5 graphs need ≥15 edges). Formalizing these would require: (1) a complete enumeration of graphs with few edges showing their dimension is ≤3; (2) a proof that K_{3,3} requires ℝ⁴ via geometric rigidity; (3) a uniqueness argument classifying all 9-edge 4-dimensional graphs. These are currently beyond what can be automated or easily proved in Lean without specialized combinatorial geometry infrastructure.
